The regex /s+/g matches the letter s instead of whitespace; it should be /\s+/g.

I reviewed it, fixed 4 bugs, added the module README and wrote the QA scenario tests/e2e/scenarios/annotate.mjs. Each annotation is a timeline feature (types pmiNote, pmiGeneralNote, pmiDimension, pmiGdt, pmiHoleNote) registered through app.M.registerFeature. Each one is listed under the PMI folder in the browser and drawn on an annotation plane in the viewport overlay (leaders, arrowheads or dots, frames, datum symbols, Arial-style text). Undo/redo, save/open, Edit Feature, suppress, roll back, rename, Show/Hide and Delete all work. I checked the dialog labels against the local Fusion string tables.

Fixes this session:
- A feature control frame attached to a dimension showed as orphaned after reopening a document.
- A boss on a cylinder that OCCT splits into several faces showed a wrong quantity ("2x").
- Custom rows in the dialogs were not indented like the framework rows.
- The Symbol dropdown caret was too large.
implemented: LeaderLineNoteCommand (Note): select a face (dot leader) or an edge/vertex (arrow leader). The note follows the cursor and a click anchors it. Rows: Change annotation plane (cycles candidate planes), Alternate annotation plane, Perpendicular text, Leader line extension, multi-line text with alignment and Insert symbol. Live preview, double-click to edit, Delete, orphan warning.
GeneralNoteCommand (General Note): text fixed to the screen in one of four quadrants (Change note quadrant), size taken from the PMI settings.

DimensionNoteCommand (Sizes and Dimensions): linear, diameter, radius and angular dimensions from 1 or 2 faces, edges or vertices. Tabs: Leader line | Dimension | Text. Modeled value or override, tolerances (symmetric, deviation, limits, fits), Measurement alignment, Angular sector, Units and precision, Secondary units, %1% text template. Names follow the type (Linear Dimension1, Diameter Dimension1, Angular Dimension1). Values follow model edits.

GeometricToleranceNoteCommand (Geometric Tolerancing): feature control frames with 14 characteristics in an image symbol menu, diameter zone, material condition, primary/secondary/tertiary datums with modifiers, free state, tangent plane, projected zone, zone, associated feature and composite control. Datum feature symbol (Create Datum, identifier, leader, extension, offset). A frame can attach to a surface or hang under an existing dimension or hole note. Uses Fusion's validation messages. Names: Flatness1, Position1, Datum A.

HoleThreadNoteCommand (Hole/Thread Note): reads Hole features (diameter, depth or THRU, counterbore, countersink, quantity) and Thread features (designation, class, direction, depth) and handles bosses. Tabs Counterbore, Countersink and Thread appear only when they apply. Each value can be overridden and toleranced. The note follows model edits and, when orphaned, keeps its last text.

FusionChangePMISettingsCmd (Change PMI Settings, in the PMI folder context menu): Standard, Size, Default Precision, Default Tolerance, Leading Zero, Trailing Zero, General Note Size, Custom General Note Size. Undoable.

build:configure.summary:
Fusion's design configurations now work end to end. The three CONFIGURE panel commands are real: Configure (FusionStartDesignConfigModeCmd), Display Configuration Table (FusionShowDesignConfigPanelCmd) and Create Configuration Rules (FusionConfigurationRulesCmd). So are the "Configure" items in the Timeline and Browser right-click menus (ConfigureFeatureCmd, ConfigureEntityCmd).

**How it behaves:**
- **Configure** opens the CONFIGURATION TABLE palette at the bottom of the canvas and enters Configuration Mode. A "CONFIGURATION ✓" bar appears at the top of the canvas (the check mark or Esc exits), timeline features and browser bodies, sketches and planes are highlighted, and a first-time intro card explains the mode.
- **Clicking a highlighted item** opens the docked CONFIGURE dialog with one check box per aspect: feature parameters and sketch dimensions, Suppression, Visibility, Appearance, Physical Material. OK adds or removes the matching table columns.
- **The table** has Parameters and Properties tabs, a row count with Add Configurations, Add Aspects, Add Parameters (a PARAMETERS dialog with a Configured column), Configuration Rules, and a More menu (sort columns and rows, export CSV). The first row is the Default Configuration; the active row is marked. Rows can be renamed, duplicated, deleted, sorted and dragged; columns can be renamed, deleted, dragged and bulk-edited (Suppress All, Invert, etc.). Cells are validated.
- **Theme tables:** Appearance Theme and Physical Material Theme tables appear under the top table.
- **Activating a configuration** (double-click a row name, the row's radio, right-click > Activate, or the searchable selector added under the BROWSER header) writes that row into the document through app.mutate. No evaluator change was needed, so undo/redo and save/open work like any other edit.
- **Edits made elsewhere** to a configured aspect (Edit Feature, Change Parameters, timeline suppress, appearance) are written back into the active configuration only, inside the same undo step.
- **Configuration Rules** is a local version of Fusion's block-based rules editor: Toolbox categories, Rule blocks with On/Off and status, if/else if/else Logic blocks, Getter, Setter, And/Or, Not, Comment. Rules run locally against every configuration: "=" drives a value (the cell becomes read-only), while min/max/range/any-of limit it. A violating edit is rejected with "Value violates rule", and Apply clamps values to the nearest allowed one.

**Results:** my configure scenario passes 97/97, and core-loop, modeling, toolbar and undo-redo all pass with zero console errors. Outside my folder I made two one-line edits, so the "Configure" right-click items in the Browser and Timeline run the real command.

notImplemented.reason: These parts of Fusion's configured-design workflow are missing: custom theme tables and Move to Theme Table, the Test Row, Sheet Metal and Plastic rule themes (this app has no such rules), component inserts and joint snaps (there are no assemblies), thread and hole-type aspect columns (only numeric hole and thread parameters can be configured), the 'Suppressed (implicit)' display, the 'Configure' tab inside modeling dialogs, and the Configured Design icon on the document tab and in the Data Panel (the app bar belongs to the shell owner).

Blocks are added by clicking a Toolbox block, which goes into the selected statement area or condition slot, and reordered with up/down buttons. Fusion uses free drag-and-drop on a Blockly canvas instead. Block From Object mode and the Workflow Guide are not built. Fusion runs rules on Autodesk's rules service; here they are evaluated locally in rules.js.

build:configure.contracts:
Full details are in src/modules/configure/README.md.

**Document data (saved with the design):**
- `doc.configurations = {version, nid, rows:[{id, name, partNumber, description}], active, columns, cells, themes, rules}`. `rows[0]` is the Default Configuration.
- Column kinds: `{kind:'param', user:true, name}`, `{kind:'param', owner, field}`, `{kind:'param', owner, cid}` (sketch dimension), `{kind:'suppress', feature}`, `{kind:'visibility', body|feature}`, `{kind:'theme', table:'appearance'|'material'}`. Optional `title` (renamed column) and `param`.
- Cell values: a parameter cell holds an expression string; suppress holds a bool (true = suppressed); visibility holds a bool (true = visible); a theme cell holds a theme row id.
- `themes.appearance` / `themes.material = {rows, columns:[{id, body}], cells}`.
- Rules: `{id, name, comment, active, body}`. Statements are set / if (with elifs and else) / comment; conditions are get / and / or / not. Getter ops: eq ne gt ge lt le range anyOf. Setter ops: eq ne min max range anyOf.

**Runtime rule:** the document's live values always show the active configuration. Any other module's edit to a configured aspect is copied into the active row on the 'doc' event (same undo step) and re-checked against the rules.

**Public API `app.ui.configure`:**
- `configured`, `configurations()`, `active()`, `columns()`
- `activate(idOrName)`, `addConfigurations(n)`, `addAspect(template)`, `setCell(row, col, value)` (validated and rule-checked)
- `configure({kind:'feature'|'body', id})`, `enterMode()` / `exitMode()`, `openRules()`, `openParameters()`, `applyRules(rules)`
- `table {visible, show, hide, toggle, render, startRename}`, `mode {active, enter, exit}`, `selector`
- `data` (data.js) and `rules` (rules.js) are pure functions usable in Node.

**Event:** `configure` with `{table: bool}` or `{mode: bool}`.

**Commands:** `ConfigureFeatureCmd` takes ctx `{id}`; `ConfigureEntityCmd` takes `{ref:{kind:'body', body}}`. Other modules can route their own "Configure" menu items to these.

**DOM hooks for tests:** `[data-cfg-table]`, `[data-cfg="count|add-configurations|add-aspects|add-parameters|rules|more|exit-mode|add-themes:<table>"]`, `[data-table="top"]`, `[data-row-name]`, `[data-col]`, `[data-input="<row>:<col>"]` (state buttons expose `data-value`), `[data-cfg-mode]`, `[data-cfg-selector-head]`, `[data-cfg-option]`, `.dlg[data-dialog="ConfigureFeatureCmd|ConfigureEntityCmd"]`, `[data-dialog="ConfigureParameters"] .cfg-pm-check[data-param]`, `[data-dialog="FusionConfigurationRulesCmd"]` (with `[data-cat]`, `[data-block]`, `[data-rule]`, `[data-rule-status]`, `[data-mutator]`).

knownIssues: Default names are inferred, not confirmed by evidence: configurations are 'Configuration N' (taken from the Fusion blog's examples) and theme rows are 'Theme N'.

The table docks along the bottom of the canvas above the nav bar, and the selector sits as a strip under the BROWSER header. Both layouts are inferred; no reference capture of Fusion's configuration UI exists on this machine, and Autodesk's help images could not be fetched.
The rules editor uses click-to-insert blocks rather than free drag-and-drop. Rules are evaluated locally, with no Fusion Design Extension entitlement check.

When a configured feature or body is deleted, its column stays and is marked '(aspect no longer exists)' until the user deletes it. Downstream features of a suppressed one are not shown as 'Suppressed (implicit)'.
Rule evaluation re-applies each configuration row to a light copy of the document (a features clone per row) for parameter values. This is fine for typical tables but grows with rows × features.
Theme tables have no root-component column (the app has no components), and Fusion's warnings when deleting a column that drives other columns are not reproduced.

Changes from the latest edits (Logic block settings flyout, the user-parameter aspect label, resetting the browser selector on New/Open) were checked by the final configure scenario run and the ad-hoc scripts. The browser, timeline, save-open, parameters, toolbox, marking-menu and shortcuts scenarios were not re-run after them; those edits are inside my own module only.
